title: Windows computer running slowly
description: Speed up a Windows 10 or 11 PC that has become sluggish, using safe and reversible steps first.
symptoms: Apps take a long time to open
Fan is loud even when idle
causes: Too many programs starting with Windows
Not enough memory (RAM) for current use
prerequisites: You are signed in with a Windows account that can change settings

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.instruction: Choose Start > Power > Restart. Do not use Shut down: with Fast Startup enabled it may not fully clear memory.
steps.expected: The PC reboots and feels responsive for the first few minutes.

steps.title: Find what is using resources
steps.instruction: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager. Click the Processes tab, then click the CPU, Memory and Disk column headers to sort. Note any app using a very high share.
steps.expected: You can see which app is the heaviest. Normal idle CPU is usually under 10%.

steps.title: Close or limit heavy apps
steps.instruction: Select the heavy app and choose End task only if it is an app you opened yourself and saved. Do not end items you do not recognise, because some are needed by Windows.
steps.expected: CPU, memory or disk use drops after the app closes.

steps.title: Reduce startup programs
steps.instruction: In Task Manager open Startup apps (Windows 11) or Startup (Windows 10). Right-click apps you do not need at sign-in and choose Disable. This does not uninstall them.
steps.expected: Next restart, Windows reaches a usable desktop faster.

steps.title: Check free space and updates
steps.instruction: Open Settings > System > Storage and confirm at least 15% of the drive is free. Then open Settings > Windows Update and install pending updates.
steps.expected: Storage shows healthy free space and Windows Update says you are up to date.

warnings: Do not download 'PC speed-up' or registry cleaner tools; they are a common source of malware and rarely help.
recovery: Any startup app you disabled can be re-enabled from the same Startup list.
alternatives: If the PC has 4 GB of RAM or less, adding memory (done by a technician if needed) often gives the biggest improvement.

title: Laptop will not turn on
description: Work out whether a dead laptop has a power, battery or display problem before seeking repair.
symptoms: No lights or fan noise when pressing power
Lights come on but the screen stays black
Laptop turns on only when plugged in

steps.title: Check the power source
steps.instruction: Plug the charger directly into a wall socket you know works (not a loose extension). Look for a charging light on the laptop or charger and check the cable for kinks or damage.
steps.expected: A charging light appears, or the laptop shows a battery icon.

steps.title: Disconnect everything else
steps.instruction: Unplug USB drives, docks, printers and external displays. A faulty accessory can stop startup.
steps.expected: The laptop has only the charger attached.

steps.title: Let it charge, then try the power button
steps.instruction: Leave it plugged in for 30 minutes, then hold the power button for 2 seconds.
steps.expected: Lights, fan noise or the manufacturer logo appear.

steps.title: Do a power reset
steps.instruction: Unplug the charger, then hold the power button for 15 to 30 seconds and release. Plug the charger back in and press power once. Do not open the laptop or remove internal parts.
steps.expected: The laptop starts, or a charging light appears where there was none.

steps.title: Check whether only the screen is dark
steps.instruction: If fans or lights run but the screen is black, shine a torch at the screen at an angle to look for a faint image, or connect an external monitor and press the display switch key (often Fn plus a screen icon, or Windows+P).
steps.expected: A picture on the external monitor means the laptop works and the internal display or its settings are the problem.

warnings: Never open a laptop or puncture, bend or pry a swollen battery. A swollen battery is a fire risk: stop using it and contact a qualified technician.
alternatives: If the laptop stays dead after a different charger and a power reset, a technician should test the battery and motherboard.

title: Laptop battery not charging
description: Find out why a laptop shows 'plugged in, not charging' or does not charge at all.

steps.title: Check the charger and port
steps.instruction: Confirm the charger wattage matches the label under the laptop. Look for bent pins, debris or loose fit at the port, and kinks in the cable. If you can, try a second compatible charger.
steps.expected: The charger fits firmly and its indicator light is on.

steps.title: Remove heat and accessories
steps.instruction: Unplug USB devices and let a hot laptop cool for 10 minutes. Many laptops pause charging when hot.
steps.expected: Charging resumes once the laptop is cool.

steps.title: Restart and check battery settings
steps.instruction: Restart with the charger connected. Check the maker's app (for example Lenovo Vantage, MyASUS or HP Support Assistant) for a battery-protection or charge-limit setting, which may hold charge at 60 to 80 percent on purpose.
steps.expected: Either the battery charges, or you learn that a limit is set deliberately.

steps.title: Update system firmware from the maker
steps.instruction: Use Windows Update or the manufacturer's own support app to install BIOS and battery-firmware updates. Do not download them from third-party sites.
steps.expected: Updates install and the charging state is re-checked.

steps.title: Judge the battery's health
steps.instruction: If the laptop only runs on the charger, or shuts down instantly when unplugged, the battery is likely worn out. A technician can test and replace it.
steps.expected: You know whether to replace the battery or the charger.

warnings: Do not use unbranded chargers and never open the battery compartment of a sealed laptop.

title: Computer connected to Wi-Fi but no internet
description: Fix the 'connected, no internet' state on a Windows or Mac computer.
symptoms: Websites will not load but the network name shows connected
Other apps cannot reach the internet
causes: Router or modem lost its internet link

steps.title: Test another device
steps.instruction: Try a phone on the same Wi-Fi. If it also has no internet, the problem is the router or the provider; go to the router guide.
steps.expected: You know if the problem is this computer or the network.

steps.title: Toggle Wi-Fi and restart
steps.instruction: Turn Wi-Fi off and on, then restart the computer.

steps.title: Forget and rejoin the network
steps.instruction: Windows: Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Forget. Mac: System Settings > Wi-Fi > Details > Forget This Network. Reconnect with the password.
steps.expected: The computer gets a fresh address and connects. Have the Wi-Fi password ready first.

steps.title: Renew the network configuration (Windows)
steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt and run: ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew then ipconfig /flushdns. These only refresh your address and clear the DNS cache; they do not delete files.
steps.expected: A new IP address is shown and websites load.

steps.title: Try a different DNS server
steps.instruction: See the DNS guide to switch to a public resolver temporarily.
steps.expected: Sites load by name if DNS was the cause.

recovery: To undo a DNS change, set DNS back to 'Automatic'.

title: Windows computer has no sound
description: Restore audio on a Windows PC by checking output, volume, and drivers in a safe order.
symptoms: No sound from speakers or headphones
Red X on the volume icon
Sound works in one app only

steps.title: Check volume and mute
steps.instruction: Click the speaker icon in the taskbar and confirm the master volume is up and not muted. Check the app's own volume too.
steps.expected: The volume slider is above zero and not muted.

steps.title: Select the right output
steps.instruction: Click the arrow beside the volume slider (or Settings > System > Sound > Output) and choose your speakers or headphones.
steps.expected: Sound plays from the chosen device.

steps.title: Check connections
steps.instruction: Re-seat headphone or speaker cables and try a different port. For Bluetooth audio, confirm the device is connected.

steps.title: Run the audio troubleshooter
steps.instruction: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Audio > Run.
steps.expected: Windows fixes or reports the issue.

steps.title: Reinstall the audio driver
steps.instruction: Open Device Manager, expand Sound, video and game controllers, right-click your audio device, choose Uninstall device, then restart. Windows reinstalls the driver on boot.

warnings: Only download drivers from your PC maker or through Windows Update.
recovery: If sound worsens after a driver update, use Device Manager > Properties > Driver > Roll Back Driver.

title: Computer running out of storage
description: Free up disk space on a Windows PC without deleting anything you need.
prerequisites: Know where your important files are

steps.title: See what is using space
steps.instruction: Open Settings > System > Storage and review the categories.
steps.expected: You know which categories are largest.

steps.title: Turn on Storage Sense
steps.instruction: In Storage, enable Storage Sense and choose Run now. It removes temporary files and empties the Recycle Bin by schedule.

steps.title: Remove unused apps
steps.instruction: Settings > Apps > Installed apps, sort by size, and uninstall apps you are certain you no longer use.
steps.expected: Disk use drops; apps can be reinstalled later.

steps.title: Move or back up large files
steps.instruction: Copy videos, photos and downloads to an external drive or a cloud service you trust, check they opened correctly, then delete the local copies.

steps.title: Empty the Recycle Bin
steps.instruction: Right-click the Recycle Bin and choose Empty only after checking nothing needed is inside.
steps.expected: Space from deleted files is released.

warnings: Never delete files from the Windows or Program Files folders to save space.
alternatives: Consider a larger or additional drive if space is always short.

title: Bluetooth not detecting devices
description: Make a computer or phone find nearby Bluetooth headphones, speakers, keyboards and mice.
symptoms: Bluetooth toggle is missing or greyed out
Device appears but will not pair
causes: Bluetooth turned off or airplane mode on

steps.title: Put the accessory in pairing mode
steps.instruction: Hold the accessory's pairing or Bluetooth button until its light flashes. Check its manual because the method differs by model.

steps.title: Confirm Bluetooth is on
steps.instruction: Turn off Airplane mode and switch Bluetooth on in Settings (Windows: Settings > Bluetooth & devices).
steps.expected: Bluetooth toggle is on and scanning.

steps.title: Move closer and remove interference
steps.instruction: Keep the devices within 1 metre, away from USB 3 hubs and microwave ovens.
steps.expected: The accessory appears in the list.

steps.title: Remove old pairings and retry
steps.instruction: Delete the accessory from the saved devices list, then add it again as a new device.

steps.title: Restart Bluetooth service or the device
steps.instruction: Restart your computer or phone. On Windows, check Device Manager for a Bluetooth section; if absent, see the manufacturer's site for chipset support.
steps.expected: The Bluetooth adapter is listed and works.

title: Application freezing or crashing
description: Stabilise a desktop program that hangs, closes itself or will not open.

steps.title: Close and reopen the app
steps.instruction: Wait one minute for it to respond, then close it (Windows: Task Manager > End task; Mac: Force Quit from the Apple menu). Reopen it.
steps.expected: The app opens normally. Unsaved work in the frozen window may be lost.

steps.title: Restart your computer
steps.instruction: A restart clears memory and stuck background processes.

steps.title: Update the app and your system
steps.instruction: Install updates for the app from its own update option or the official store, then install system updates.

steps.title: Check free memory and disk space
steps.instruction: Keep at least 10 to 15% of the disk free and close other heavy programs.
steps.expected: Fewer crashes with fewer programs running.

steps.title: Repair or reinstall
steps.instruction: Windows: Settings > Apps > Installed apps > your app > Advanced options > Repair. If that fails, uninstall and reinstall from the official source after backing up any app data.

warnings: Back up documents the app created before uninstalling it.

title: USB device not recognized
description: Get Windows to detect a USB drive, printer, keyboard or other device.
symptoms: Drive does not appear in File Explorer

steps.title: Try another port and cable
steps.instruction: Unplug the device and connect it to a different port directly on the computer, not through a hub.

steps.title: Test it on another computer
steps.instruction: If it fails there too, the device or cable is faulty.
steps.expected: You know whether the device or this PC is at fault.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.instruction: Disconnect the device, restart, then reconnect.

steps.title: Check Device Manager
steps.instruction: Open Device Manager and look for items with a yellow warning icon. Right-click > Uninstall device, unplug the USB device, restart and reconnect.

steps.title: Disable USB power saving
steps.instruction: Settings > System > Power & battery > Power mode, and in Device Manager open each USB Root Hub > Power Management and untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'.

warnings: If a drive holds important files, do not click Format when Windows offers it. Contact a data-recovery professional.

title: Windows update failing
description: Resolve Windows Update errors using the built-in troubleshooter and safe repair tools.

steps.title: Free space and stay connected
steps.instruction: Make sure at least 20 GB is free and the PC is plugged in. Pause other downloads.
steps.expected: Update has the room and power it needs.

steps.title: Restart and retry
steps.instruction: Restart, then Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates.

steps.title: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter
steps.instruction: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update > Run.
steps.expected: Troubleshooter reports fixes or no problem.

steps.title: Check system files
steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run: sfc /scannow. It scans protected Windows files and repairs damaged ones from a local cache. If it reports unfixable files, run: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth, then sfc /scannow again.
steps.expected: Scan reports no integrity violations or that it repaired files.

steps.title: Restart and install again
steps.instruction: Restart and run Windows Update once more.

warnings: Do not switch the PC off while an update says 'Do not turn off your computer'.
Back up important files before major updates.
alternatives: Use the official Windows Update Assistant from microsoft.com if a feature update repeatedly fails.

title: Laptop overheating
description: Cool down a hot, noisy laptop and reduce shutdowns caused by heat.

steps.title: Move to a hard, flat surface
steps.instruction: Never use it on a bed or sofa. Raise the back slightly with a stand to improve airflow.

steps.title: Check the vents
steps.instruction: Look at the side and bottom vents for lint. With the laptop off and unplugged, blow short bursts of air across the vents, or gently use a soft brush.

steps.title: Close heavy programs
steps.instruction: Open Task Manager (Windows) or Activity Monitor (Mac) and close apps using a lot of CPU.

steps.title: Update software and firmware
steps.instruction: Install OS and maker updates; they can include fan-control fixes.

steps.title: Know when to seek help
steps.instruction: If it still overheats or shuts down, a technician can clean internal dust and replace thermal paste.

warnings: Do not open the laptop or spray liquids or compressed-air cans held upside down into it.

title: Computer restarting unexpectedly
description: Investigate a Windows PC that reboots or shows a blue screen without warning.
symptoms: Blue screen with a stop code
Restart happens during gaming or heavy use

steps.title: Note when it happens
steps.instruction: Write down what you were doing and any blue-screen stop code (for example CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED).
steps.expected: A pattern or code to search for.

steps.title: Check heat
steps.instruction: Feel the vents and listen to fans. Follow the overheating guide if the machine is hot.

steps.title: Install updates
steps.instruction: Run Windows Update and install optional driver updates the maker lists. Remove recently installed software that began the problem.

steps.title: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic
steps.instruction: Search for Windows Memory Diagnostic, choose Restart now, and let the test finish. Save your work first.
steps.expected: The result says no problems, or it names a memory fault.

steps.title: Check the system files
steps.instruction: Run sfc /scannow in an administrator Command Prompt (it only repairs Windows files).

warnings: A PC that restarts constantly may be about to lose its storage. Back up important files now.
alternatives: Failing power supplies or memory modules need a qualified technician.

title: Android phone running slowly
description: Make a laggy Android phone faster with updates, storage cleanup and app management.
symptoms: Phone gets warm during simple tasks

steps.title: Restart the phone
steps.instruction: Hold the power button and choose Restart.
steps.expected: Phone feels quicker immediately after restart.

steps.title: Free storage space
steps.instruction: Settings > Storage. Remove unused apps, large videos and downloads, or move photos to a cloud account you trust first.
steps.expected: At least 10% of storage is free.

steps.title: Update Android and apps
steps.instruction: Settings > System > System update (path varies by maker), then open Google Play > Profile > Manage apps & device > Update all.

steps.title: Check for a problem app
steps.instruction: Settings > Battery or Apps shows which apps use the most battery or memory. Update, restrict background use for, or uninstall the heaviest unnecessary app.
steps.expected: The phone speeds up after removing the culprit.

steps.title: Test in Safe Mode
steps.instruction: Hold the power button, then touch and hold Power off and choose OK for Safe Mode. If the phone is fast there, a downloaded app is the cause. Restart normally to leave Safe Mode.
steps.expected: You can tell whether third-party apps are responsible.

warnings: Avoid 'cleaner' or 'booster' apps; many show ads or collect data.
alternatives: If still slow after these steps, a factory reset can help, but only after a full backup. See the warning in the reset instructions of your maker.

title: iPhone storage almost full
description: Free space on an iPhone without losing photos or data you care about.
symptoms: Cannot take photos or update iOS
prerequisites: Wi-Fi if you plan to back up to iCloud

steps.title: Review storage
steps.instruction: Settings > General > iPhone Storage and read the recommendations.
steps.expected: You see which items use the most space.

steps.title: Back up photos before deleting
steps.instruction: Turn on iCloud Photos or copy photos to a computer. Confirm they appear there before you delete anything.
steps.expected: Photos exist in a second place.

steps.title: Offload unused apps
steps.instruction: In iPhone Storage tap an app, then Offload App. This removes the app but keeps its documents and data so reinstalling restores them.
steps.expected: Space is freed and the app icon stays.

steps.title: Clear Messages and downloads
steps.instruction: Settings > General > iPhone Storage > Messages > Review Large Attachments. Delete items you do not need. In Safari, Settings > Safari > Clear History and Website Data if needed.

steps.title: Empty Recently Deleted
steps.instruction: In Photos > Albums > Recently Deleted, choose Select > Delete All. These are removed permanently.

warnings: Deleting items from Recently Deleted cannot be undone.
recovery: Offloaded apps can be reinstalled from the App Store with their data intact.

title: Phone battery draining quickly
description: Find what is draining an Android phone or iPhone battery and reduce the drain.
symptoms: Battery falls by several percent per hour on standby
Battery lasts under half a day

steps.title: See which apps use the most
steps.instruction: Android: Settings > Battery > Battery usage. iPhone: Settings > Battery. Look at the top apps in the last 24 hours.

steps.title: Restrict background activity
steps.instruction: For heavy apps limit background use (Android: App info > Battery > Restricted; iPhone: Settings > General > Background App Refresh).

steps.title: Adjust screen and connections
steps.instruction: Lower brightness, enable auto-brightness, shorten screen timeout, and turn off Bluetooth and location when not needed.

steps.title: Update the system and apps
steps.instruction: Install the latest OS and app updates; they often contain battery fixes.

steps.title: Check battery health
steps.instruction: iPhone: Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging. Android: Settings > Battery > Battery health (where offered) or Samsung Members. Below about 80% maximum capacity, replacement from the manufacturer or an authorised service provider may be worthwhile.
steps.expected: You know if the battery is worn.

warnings: Do not replace a sealed phone battery yourself.

title: Phone overheating
description: Cool a hot Android phone or iPhone safely and reduce future heat.
symptoms: Screen dims or a temperature warning appears
causes: Charging while in a thick case

steps.title: Stop heavy use and unplug
steps.instruction: Close apps, unplug the charger and remove the case.

steps.title: Move to a cool, shaded place
steps.instruction: Place the phone on a table in shade. Do not put it in a fridge, freezer or ice; sudden cold causes condensation.
steps.expected: It cools gradually to normal warmth.

steps.title: Turn on power saving
steps.instruction: Enable Battery Saver (Android) or Low Power Mode (iPhone) and lower brightness.

steps.title: Update and find the heavy app
steps.instruction: Update the OS and apps. Check Settings > Battery for apps that are using lots of power while idle.
steps.expected: A problem app is identified or fixed.

steps.title: Check the charger and cable
steps.instruction: Use a quality charger from the phone maker or a certified brand and look for a bent or loose port.
steps.expected: The phone stays cool while charging.

warnings: If the phone swells, smells, smokes or becomes too hot to hold, turn it off, keep it away from flammable materials and contact the manufacturer.

title: Phone applications crashing
description: Stop apps on Android or iPhone from closing themselves or failing to open.
symptoms: Error message about the app stopping

steps.title: Close and reopen the app
steps.instruction: Swipe the app away from the app switcher and open it again.

steps.title: Restart the phone
steps.instruction: Power off and on.

steps.title: Update the app and OS
steps.instruction: Update the app from Google Play or the App Store, and install the latest system update.

steps.title: Clear the app cache (Android) or offload (iPhone)
steps.instruction: Android: Settings > Apps > the app > Storage > Clear cache. Do not choose Clear data unless you accept losing app data. iPhone: Settings > General > iPhone Storage > the app > Offload App then reinstall.

steps.title: Reinstall the app
steps.instruction: Uninstall and install again from the official store. Make sure you know your login details first.

warnings: Clear data or deleting an app can remove local data that is not backed up.

title: Phone unable to connect to Wi-Fi
description: Reconnect an Android phone or iPhone that cannot join or stay on a Wi-Fi network.

steps.title: Check basics
steps.instruction: Turn off Airplane mode, switch Wi-Fi off and on, and move closer to the router.
steps.expected: Network name appears and signal is strong.

steps.title: Re-enter the password
steps.instruction: Forget the network (Android: tap the network > Forget; iPhone: tap the i icon > Forget This Network) and rejoin. Check upper and lower case characters carefully.

steps.title: Test another device
steps.instruction: If other devices also fail, restart the router (see the router guide).
steps.expected: You know whether the phone or the router is at fault.

steps.title: Restart the phone
steps.instruction: Restart and reconnect.

steps.title: Reset network settings if nothing works
steps.instruction: Android: Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth. iPhone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings. This removes all saved Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth pairings but not your files.
steps.expected: Wi-Fi works again; you must re-enter Wi-Fi passwords.

warnings: Resetting network settings removes saved Wi-Fi passwords and pairings, so make sure you know them.

title: Bluetooth headphones not connecting
description: Pair or reconnect Bluetooth headphones and earbuds with a phone or computer.

steps.title: Charge them and turn off other devices
steps.instruction: Charge the headphones and turn off Bluetooth on other nearby devices they usually pair with.

steps.title: Enter pairing mode
steps.instruction: Hold the pairing button until the light flashes. Check the manual for the exact steps.

steps.title: Forget and re-pair
steps.instruction: In your device's Bluetooth settings choose the headphones > Forget or Remove, then scan and pair again.

steps.title: Choose them as the audio output
steps.instruction: On a computer, select the headphones in the sound output list.

steps.title: Reset the headphones
steps.instruction: Look up the factory-reset method in the manual. It typically clears pairings only. Re-pair afterwards.

title: Phone not charging
description: Diagnose why an Android phone or iPhone does not charge or charges very slowly.

steps.title: Swap cable, adapter and outlet
steps.instruction: Try a different cable, adapter and wall socket. Prefer the maker's accessories or certified ones.

steps.title: Inspect the port
steps.instruction: Power the phone off. Use a torch to look for lint. Gently remove it with a non-metal tool such as a wooden toothpick. Do not use liquids, metal pins or compressed air.

steps.title: Restart or force restart
steps.instruction: Android: hold power and choose Restart. iPhone: press and release volume up, press and release volume down, then hold the side button until the Apple logo appears (for Face ID models and iPhone SE 3rd generation).

steps.title: Let it charge for 30 minutes
steps.instruction: A deeply drained phone may take several minutes before showing a charging icon.

steps.title: Get the port or battery checked
steps.instruction: If it still does not charge, contact the manufacturer or an authorised repair shop. Do not open the phone.

warnings: Never use a damaged cable or a phone that is swollen or smells hot.

title: Mobile hotspot not working
description: Share your phone's mobile data with a laptop or other device when the hotspot fails.
symptoms: Devices connect but get no internet
prerequisites: A mobile plan that includes hotspot data

steps.title: Check mobile data and plan
steps.instruction: Confirm the phone itself can browse on mobile data and your plan includes tethering.

steps.title: Turn the hotspot off and on
steps.instruction: Android: Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering. iPhone: Settings > Personal Hotspot. Toggle off and on and keep the settings screen open while connecting.

steps.title: Adjust compatibility settings
steps.instruction: iPhone: turn on Maximize Compatibility. Android: switch the AP band to 2.4 GHz. Older laptops may not see 5 GHz.

steps.title: Turn off battery saver
steps.instruction: Battery saver can disable hotspot. Switch it off or plug in the phone.

steps.title: Reset network settings
steps.instruction: Only if needed, reset network settings (see the phone Wi-Fi guide). This removes saved Wi-Fi networks.
steps.expected: Hotspot works after setting it up again.

title: Files not transferring between phone and computer
description: Make a computer see a phone's files over USB so photos and documents can be copied.
symptoms: Phone charges but is not shown on the computer
causes: USB mode set to charging only

steps.title: Use a data-capable cable
steps.instruction: Some cables only charge. Try the cable that came with the phone or another data cable.
steps.expected: The computer plays a connection sound.

steps.title: Unlock the phone and allow access
steps.instruction: Android: swipe down, tap the USB notification and choose File transfer. iPhone: tap Trust when asked and enter your passcode.
steps.expected: Phone appears as a drive or in the Photos app.

steps.title: Use the right app
steps.instruction: Windows: This PC for Android or Photos > Import for iPhone. Mac with Android: use Android File Transfer from Google. Mac with iPhone: use Finder, Photos or AirDrop.
steps.expected: You can browse and copy files.

steps.title: Update and restart
steps.instruction: Restart phone and computer, and install system updates. On Windows with iPhone, install Apple Devices from the Microsoft Store.

steps.title: Use a wireless alternative
steps.instruction: Send files with AirDrop (Apple), Quick Share (Android and Windows) or a trusted cloud service.

title: Router appears connected but there is no internet
description: Restore internet when every device shows Wi-Fi but nothing loads.
symptoms: All devices show Wi-Fi but no websites load
Router internet light is red or off
Problem started after a power cut
causes: Modem or router needs a restart
tools: Phone with mobile data to check provider status

steps.title: Check for an outage
steps.instruction: Use your phone's mobile data to check your provider's outage page or social account, or call them.
steps.expected: You know if there is an area outage.

steps.title: Check cables and lights
steps.instruction: Make sure the cable from the wall or modem is firmly seated in the router's internet (WAN) port, and note which lights are red or off.

steps.title: Restart modem and router in order
steps.instruction: Unplug power from the modem and router. Wait 60 seconds. Plug in the modem first, wait until its lights are stable (about 2 minutes), then plug in the router and wait 2 minutes.
steps.expected: The internet light turns solid and devices get online.

steps.title: Test with a cable
steps.instruction: Connect a computer to the router with an Ethernet cable. If it works, the problem is Wi-Fi and not the connection.
steps.expected: You can separate wired and wireless faults.

steps.title: Contact your provider
steps.instruction: If lights remain red after a restart, give your provider the light pattern. Do not hold the router reset button unless instructed because it erases settings.

warnings: Resetting the router to factory defaults erases the Wi-Fi name, password and any provider login details.

title: Slow Wi-Fi connection
description: Improve slow or unstable Wi-Fi speeds at home using placement, bands and device checks.

steps.title: Test speed near the router
steps.instruction: Run a speed test in the same room as the router, then in the slow room. Compare with your plan's advertised speed.
steps.expected: You know if distance or the plan is the issue.

steps.title: Move the router
steps.instruction: Place it in a central, raised, open spot away from microwaves, thick walls and metal.

steps.title: Use the right band
steps.instruction: Use 5 GHz for speed at short range and 2.4 GHz for range through walls.

steps.title: Reduce device load
steps.instruction: Pause large downloads, cloud backups and streaming on other devices.
steps.expected: Speed rises for the device you are using.

steps.title: Restart and update
steps.instruction: Restart the router and install firmware updates through its official admin page.

alternatives: A mesh Wi-Fi system or wired access point can help large homes.

title: DNS resolution errors
description: Fix 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN' and similar errors when sites will not load by name.
symptoms: Error saying the server's DNS address could not be found
Sites load by IP but not by name
Some sites load, others do not

steps.title: Test another device and site
steps.instruction: Try another site and device. If all fail, restart the router first.
steps.expected: You know if the fault is local.

steps.title: Flush the DNS cache
steps.instruction: Windows: run ipconfig /flushdns in Command Prompt. macOS: run sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder. These only clear stored lookups.

steps.title: Turn off VPN or filter temporarily
steps.instruction: Pause any VPN or DNS filter you installed yourself, then retry. Turn it back on afterwards.
steps.expected: Sites load if it was interfering.

steps.title: Try a public DNS server
steps.instruction: Windows: Settings > Network & internet > your network > DNS server assignment > Edit > Manual, set Preferred DNS to 1.1.1.1 and Alternate to 8.8.8.8 (Cloudflare and Google).

steps.title: Return to Automatic if it did not help
steps.instruction: Change DNS back to Automatic (DHCP) and contact your provider.

warnings: Public DNS is optional and means the chosen company sees your domain lookups. Pick one you trust.
recovery: Set DNS server assignment back to Automatic.

title: Laptop unable to detect a wireless network
description: Bring back the list of Wi-Fi networks on a laptop that shows none.
symptoms: Wi-Fi switch missing or greyed out
causes: Airplane mode or hardware Wi-Fi switch
Router set to hidden or a band the laptop cannot see

steps.title: Turn off Airplane mode and check keys
steps.instruction: Disable Airplane mode in Settings. Also look for a Wi-Fi key (Fn plus an antenna or aeroplane symbol) or a physical switch on the side.
steps.expected: The Wi-Fi toggle can be turned on.

steps.title: Check the adapter
steps.instruction: Windows: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings. If Wi-Fi is Disabled, choose Enable.

steps.title: Restart the laptop and router
steps.instruction: Restart both. If other devices cannot see the network, the router is the cause.

steps.title: Update or reinstall the Wi-Fi driver
steps.instruction: Install updates via Windows Update or the maker's support site. In Device Manager > Network adapters, right-click the Wi-Fi adapter > Uninstall device, then restart.

steps.title: Use the network reset only if needed
steps.instruction: Windows: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset. This removes saved networks and reinstalls adapters.
steps.expected: Wi-Fi settings return to defaults; you will re-enter passwords.

warnings: Network reset removes saved Wi-Fi networks and VPN settings.

title: Bluetooth connection frequently disconnecting
description: Stabilise Bluetooth audio, mice and keyboards that keep dropping their connection.
symptoms: Device disconnects after a few minutes

steps.title: Charge the accessory and shorten the distance
steps.instruction: Charge or replace batteries and keep the devices close with no thick obstacles.

steps.title: Reduce interference
steps.instruction: Move away from USB 3 hubs, Wi-Fi routers and microwaves; connect fewer Bluetooth devices at once.

steps.title: Disable Bluetooth power saving
steps.instruction: Windows: Device Manager > Bluetooth adapter > Properties > Power Management > untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'.

steps.title: Re-pair the device
steps.instruction: Remove it from the saved list and pair again.

steps.title: Update software
steps.instruction: Install OS, driver and accessory firmware updates from official sources.
